newsitem.title: USA: J.C. Penney buys Eckerd for $2.54 billion in cash/stock.
newsitem.headline: J.C. Penney buys Eckerd for $2.54 billion in cash/stock.

text.p: Consolidation of the nation's drugstore industry took another step forward Sunday with the announcement by J.C. Penney, owner of the Thrift drugstore chain, that it agreed to buy Eckerd Corp. for cash and stock valued at $2.54 billion.
With the addition of $760 million in Eckerd debt, the deal is valued at $3.3 billion, the companies said.
The acquisition would be Penney's second in the rapidly consolidating drugstore industry since August, when it agreed to buy Fay's Inc. for about $285 million.

It follows last week's agreement by Drugstore giant Revco D.S. Inc. to buy regional chain Big B Inc. in a sweetened takeover valued at $380 million, and a deal earlier last month in which Rite Aid Corp. signed an agreement to buy West Coast chain Thrifty PayLess Inc. for $1.4 billion.
Eckerd had been viewed as a possible bidder for Big B, which had rejected Revco's initial offer.
Rite Aid had signed a pact to buy Revco for $1.8 billion, but that deal collapsed after regulators expressed concern that the union would raise consumer prices.
